title: Transporting Nutrients and Water
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Transporting Nutrients and Water Worksheets (Digestion and Blood)
standard_text: Describe the ways in which nutrients and water are transported within animals, including humans.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on transporting nutrients and water: the digestive system, absorption in the small intestine, blood plasma, water balance and the kidneys. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Digested food rides in the blood.
key_sub: Nutrients enter the blood in the small intestine and travel to every cell.
body_html:
How to think about it

Food is broken down, absorbed into the blood, and carried to every cell.

  • Path: mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum.
  • Nutrients pass through the walls of the small intestine into the blood. Water is taken back in the large intestine.
  • The heart pumps blood; the plasma carries nutrients and water to the cells. Kidneys remove waste and extra water.
Example

Where do nutrients enter the blood?

Food is broken down in the stomach

Absorbed through the small intestine walls

Answer: the small intestine

Example

4 glasses of 250 ml. Total?

4 × 250

Answer: 1,000 ml

Common mistakes

  • Thinking food goes down the windpipe.
  • Thinking nutrients are absorbed in the stomach.
  • Thinking water only leaves the body in urine.

faq.q: How are nutrients transported in the body?
faq.a: Food is digested into small pieces, absorbed through the walls of the small intestine into the blood, and the heart pumps the blood to every cell.
Mostly in the large intestine, where water is taken back from the leftover waste. Blood then carries water around the body.

faq.q: How does the body lose water?
faq.a: In urine made by the kidneys, in sweat, and in the water vapour we breathe out.
